subject.title: [Bug]: `exec` tool does not inherit `skills.entries.*.env` environment variables

question: Should explicitly configured `skills.entries.<skill>.env` credential-shaped keys be allowed into host exec child processes by default, or should they require skill metadata/declaration first?
rationale: The current code protects the host exec boundary by blocking credential-shaped env names unless metadata declares them, while the reported bug needs operator-configured keys such as `GOG_KEYRING_PASSWORD` to pass through.

options.title: Allow explicit per-skill env keys
options.body: Treat keys the operator placed in `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as trusted for host runs, while preserving the hard blocklist for host-execution control variables and adding focused regression coverage.

options.title: Require metadata declaration
options.body: Keep the current metadata-only sensitive-key allowlist and update docs/doctor output so users know skills must declare credential env names before scoped injection works.

options.title: Add an opt-in strict/allow mode
options.body: Preserve the current default and add a documented operator-controlled setting for trusted skills that need credential-shaped per-skill env injection.

recommendation.title: Allow explicit per-skill env keys
recommendation.body: Treat keys the operator placed in `skills.entries.<skill>.env` as trusted for host runs, while preserving the hard blocklist for host-execution control variables and adding focused regression coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the skill env sanitizer behavior whose trust boundary needs confirmation.
